reply_text:
Understood. The difference seems to be where the checking happens. In the APM Machine, acceptance mostly rested on what the agents reported. The solver's report carried a `:statement-unchanged?` field that it filled in itself. The topology loop's only statement check was a line in the review prompt asking the reviewer to recompute hashes. That's how 18 closed problems ended up with weakened statements, and nothing caught it. The parks, frames and cascade were built on top of those reports, so a report that was wrong passed through all of them.

The solve loop is about 300 lines. The seat never touches the repository. The script itself runs the compile and the `sorry` count, reads `#print axioms`, and compares the statement fingerprint with the one pinned at dispatch. Agents only supply a file, and everything the loop accepts, it has checked itself.

It hasn't proved anything yet, though. The first real test is whether the 51 queued problems start closing under it. If the loop surfaces stuck problems or false statements the way the route review did today, that tells us something too.

I've saved your view as a memory: default to plain loops whose checks the script computes, and don't propose parks or cascades unless you ask. I agree the War Machine should keep its parks machinery to the minimum it actually needs.
